newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen rangebound, demand thin.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen rangebound, demand thin.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Monday were expected to stay within range as crude eases amid ample supplies, traders said.
Centistoke 180 prices were quoted at $116-$118 per tonne on Friday for November loading supplies from Singapore on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
Traders said the market is slugglish with very little enquiries heard from buyers.
They expected the market to continue to be well-offered with South Korean supplies still unsold while demand from China and Indonesia remained thin.
"If there is a bid at $115 which is a good bid, I bet there would be an offer out there," said a trader.
"I think the market would stay within the current range," said another trader.
India has awarded its tender to buy 14,000 tonnes for November 15-18 delivery at below $6.50 per tonne premia over Mideast quotes on a fob basis to Swiss trader, Glencore.
